title: Acceleration & Strength
summary: Session 1 went perfectly: 41/41 sets, nothing missed or cut short. Same session again with a small step up everywhere: pogos to 20, box jumps to 4, a bit more weight on the lifts. Broad jumps stay on hold, and there's a quick single-leg calf raise test at the end of accessories to see how close he is to bringing them back.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.cue: Injured side as front leg: let the knee drift forward over the toes slowly. If the front of the ankle pinches, stop short of it.

exercises.name: Calf Raises (double then single leg)
exercises.cue: Same primer as session 1, before pogos: 10 double-leg, then 10 single-leg on the injured side.

exercises.name: Pogo Jumps
exercises.cue: Up from 3×15, which he did cleanly last time. Stiff ankles, quiet even landings. If the last 5 reps get flat-footed or lopsided, stop at 15.

exercises.name: Falling Start Accels
exercises.cue: Pain-free last time, so full effort from the first rep after a build-up run. Lean, fall, drive.

exercises.name: Box Jump (instead of Broad Jump)
exercises.cue: Up from 3×3. Jump up, step down. Land soft and level on the box.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
exercises.cue: Still held. Comes back as a broad jump with a 2-second stuck landing once the calf raise test (block E) reaches about 25.

exercises.name: Chin Ups
exercises.cue: Up from 4×6. If the 4th set stalls at 6, that's fine.

exercises.name: DB Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Injured leg as the front leg: control the knee travel forward rather than dropping into the bottom.

exercises.name: DB Bench Press
exercises.cue: Go to 25 kg; if 10 isn't there, 8 is fine.
exercises.extra: RPE 7 · last 3 × 10 × 22.5 kg (a PB, best was 8)

exercises.name: DB Calf Raise (single leg)
exercises.cue: Still the most useful exercise for the ankle. Same 15 kg, two more reps. Slow 3-second lower, full range.
exercises.extra: RPE 7 · last 3 × 10 × 15 kg · can use a machine

exercises.name: Calf Raise Test (injured side)
exercises.cue: After the last calf set and a 2-minute rest: bodyweight only, single leg on the injured side, full range, steady tempo. Stop when height drops off. Then do the good side. Log both in a note. About 25 on the injured side, close to the good side, means broad jumps can start coming back.

exercises.name: Split Stance Cable Pallof Press
exercises.cue: Do sets with each leg in front. One plate heavier than last time.

next: Pogos: 3×20 → forward/back and side-to-side pogos → single-leg pogos.
Broad jumps: box jumps → broad jump with a 2-second stuck landing → full broad jumps.
Ready for broad jumps when pogos feel easy and even, sprints are pain-free, and the calf raise test gets to about 25 on the injured side.
Box squat: keep adding 2.5–5 kg a session while RPE stays at 7 or under.
